conviction_note: Evidence nearly offsets. Industrial demand is strong (Fastenal Q3 +15.5% DSR, ISM 54.5, 3M's own Q2 orders +10% and backlog +20%). Against that, Brent averaged $114 in September against roughly $88 when 3M set its $150-175m oil-inflation estimate, and PC/device production is weak. So p_up sits at 52 on an abs move of 6.5 (implied 5.59, own median 6.96). The findings sum to +0.15, and the two measurements agree that there is no meaningful lean.

findings.finding: Fastenal's Q3 2026 release (14 Oct, after 3M last spoke) shows daily sales +15.5% y/y, with manufacturing +17.2% (heavy manufacturing +20.2%) and indirect safety +13.0% against +10.6% a year earlier. Pricing contributed only ~240bp, so volume is strong. ISM manufacturing printed 54.5 in September, a ninth month of expansion. That is a strong read for 3M's Safety & Industrial segment (~47% of sales, +8.2% organic in Q2) against a FY organic guide of only >3.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: organic +5.4% and S&I +8.2% came with a beat-and-raise, and the stock rose +7.32%. In Jan 2026 (-6.96%) and Apr 2026 (-1.94%), beats without a meaningful raise were sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Fastenal is a public print a week old, and consensus Q3 revenue of $6.61bn implies only ~2% sequential growth from $6.5bn in Q2. If the read-through were priced, the 3M estimate would have moved up after 14 Oct. Zacks reports only a one-cent rise over 60 days, and the stock's 20-day run-up is negative. This is a distributor proxy, not 3M's own number.
findings.independence: ISM September PMI 54.5, new orders 55.3 (https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-pmi-reports/pmi/september/). Separate source, same direction.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (21 Jul) 3M said Q2 orders were up ~10%, backlog up nearly 20%, and the first two weeks of Q3 orders and backlog 'look good'. About 75% of the business is book-and-ship. Price was expected to rise to ~2% in H2, from 1.6% in Q2. This supports organic growth in Q3 above the 'high threes' H2 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 organic beat plus raise: +7.32%. Q3 2025: +7.66%. Earlier 2026 beats were sold (-6.96%, -1.94%), so a quarter beat alone does not reliably pay.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is the company's own public commentary, and consensus already sits ~5c above the guide-implied Q3. What is not visibly priced is a guide raise. A market expecting another raise would show a positive run-up into the print, and the 20-day run-up is -0.45%.
findings.independence: Fastenal Q3 (https://finviz.com/news/402232/fastenal-company-reports-2026-third-quarter-earnings) points the same way from a different source. It is a different document from the finding above, so the two do not double-count.

findings.finding: Brent averaged $114 in September and $95.95 for Q3 (EIA October STEO), peaking at $131 on 15 Sep, with Q4 forecast at $104.69. When 3M raised its oil-based inflation estimate to $150-175m on 21 Jul (from $125m), Brent was ~$88. Management said pricing offsets the cost in dollars but leaves a ~20bp margin drag, so a Q4 oil step-up threatens the H2 margin-expansion guide of ~100bp. It also makes a further FY raise less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock trades on the guide. The July 2026 raise bought +7.32%, while the January 2026 print with a guide below Street sold off -6.96% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Oil is public. The transmission to 3M's own inflation number is not confirmed by the company, and the consensus FY EPS still sits inside the $8.80-8.95 range. JPMorgan's target cut on 9 Oct (below) may partly reflect it. If it were fully priced, FY estimates would have been trimmed toward the low end of the guide, and no source shows that.
findings.independence: Company sensitivity is from the Q2 call (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/3m-co/earnings/2026-q2), and Brent around July 20-21 was ~$88.96 (https://www.oilmonster.com/crude-oil-prices/brent-price/225/9). This is a macro-to-company inference, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: IDC's preliminary data shows Q3 2026 PC shipments down 20.1% y/y (Omdia: -21.2%) on memory shortages. 3M had guided H2 device/PC/tablet production down 'high teens' and called it its main watch item, so the outcome lands slightly worse than the guide in Transportation & Electronics' consumer-electronics business.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No specific history found for a consumer-electronics miss at 3M. T&E grew 5.9% organic in Q2 despite consumer electronics falling low single digits.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because the outcome lands close to what the company guided. The residual is the gap between 'high teens' and -20%. Net of the rest of the company, consumer electronics is a small slice of T&E, so the finding stays small.
findings.independence: Omdia, -21.2% y/y, cited in the same search. Same direction, different firm.

findings.finding: As of the Q2 call, 3M had received no IEEPA tariff refunds while carrying ~$110m a quarter of tariff and stranded costs. By Q3, refunds were flowing across the market: 40+ S&P companies reported ~$9.6bn (WSJ via investinglive), and Mohawk put refunds inside its adjusted Q3 guide. A Q3 refund recognition at 3M is possible but unconfirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No 3M history. Across the repo's resolved names, refunds landed and the stock followed the guide direction instead.
findings.source_date: 2026 (Q3 reporting season, exact date not read)
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has barely moved (+1c over 60 days), so no refund is visibly in the estimate. 3M has said nothing about the size of an IEEPA claim, and EDGAR full-text search finds no 'IEEPA' in 3M filings in 2026. A one-off with no stated path to the guide is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Company statement of no refunds to date: https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/3m-co/earnings/2026-q2. Mohawk guide including refunds: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000851968/000085196826000031/a2026q2pressreleaseandtabl.htm

findings.finding: JPMorgan cut its 3M price target to $185 from $205 on 9 Oct 2026 and kept Overweight. No reason was published in the sources found.
findings.why_not_priced: It is on the wire, so it is largely priced. It is filed because a pre-print cut from a bull may signal a lower FY bar at a top industrials desk. The stock rose 1.5% on the day, per ad-hoc-news.
findings.independence: Goldesel reports the same cut (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/3m-aktie-kursziel-sinkt-auf-185-us-dollar-overweight-rating-bleibt), from the same underlying event.

findings.finding: Madison Fire & Rescue closed on 1 July into a majority-owned JV with Scott SCBA: ~$800m revenue, growing high single digits, margins above the company average, and $700m cash received. It was excluded from the July guide and management said it 'will be included in the Q3 call'. That gives a mechanical sales-guide uplift with EPS 'not material'.
findings.why_not_priced: A mechanical inclusion is known in principle. It is filed because a headline revenue-guide step-up can read as a raise even when EPS is unchanged. It is small because management called it immaterial to EPS.
findings.independence: This shares a document with the second finding, but it is a different fact on a different line.

findings.finding: 3M renewed its $4.25bn five-year revolver on 17 Aug (replacing an identical 2023 facility) and issued €1.5bn of notes at 3.50-4.10% on 10 Sep for general corporate purposes, including refinancing.
findings.why_not_priced: The answer to what the money buys is routine refinancing of an investment-grade balance sheet: the revolver replaces a same-size facility, and the notes refinance debt. There is no distress signal and no ramp, so the impact is zero.

findings.finding: In August 2026 a federal court in New Jersey approved the >$2.5bn PFAS settlement, under which 3M pays $400-450m over 25 years. It is a non-operating PFAS item excluded from adjusted EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PFAS items sit below adjusted operating income, and recent prints traded on the guide instead.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (date as reported in search, not read from the URL)
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced and small: spread over 25 years and excluded from adjusted figures. It is filed only for completeness.

baseline_tension: The evidence is close to balanced: a small positive from demand read-throughs and a small negative from oil on the guide. That matches a balanced skew (+1.49) and a flat 20-day run-up, so nothing cuts strongly against the market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): the Fastenal/ISM read-through to 3M is unconfirmed transmission, so it went from +1.0 to +0.8. The oil-to-guide inference went from -1.2 to -1.0 for the same reason.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold beats in Jan and Apr 2026): the backlog/orders reported-quarter finding went from +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the IEEPA refund has no stated path to the guide, so it went from +0.4 to +0.25.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the revolver and euro notes are refinancing with no distress, so they stay at 0.
Lesson 6 (bar): consensus agrees across 3-4 sources at $2.38-2.41, so no cap was needed. I noted that consensus sits above the company-implied ~$2.34.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest is ~1.8% of shares at 3.1 days, so there is no squeeze adjustment to the negatives.
Scaled measurement: p_up moved from 53 to 52 after the proxy and inference findings were shrunk. abs_move_pct is unchanged at 6.5.
